doe-osti-2585529-brine-availability-test:
Kristopher Kuhlman leads a nine-author team from Sandia, Los Alamos, and Lawrence Berkeley national laboratories in this final closeout report, SAND2025-08175R, dated July 7, 2025. The Brine Availability Test in Salt studies how brine moves in bedded salt around heated waste. The work supports plans to dispose of spent fuel and high-level waste in salt formations, under the Department of Energy's Office of Nuclear Energy.

The closeout gathers results from heated boreholes sealed with packers deep in salt. In one borehole pair, humidity behind the packer rose in the un pumped hole as heating went on, which the team links to brine pooling there and slowly wetting the seals. A sister hole, emptied often by vacuum pump, behaved in a different way. Melissa Mills, Charles Choens, Philip Stauffer, and colleagues from the three labs share authorship.
doe-osti-2999897-advanced-moderator-mate:
Caitlin Kohnert, William Neilson, Nedim Cinbiz and many contributors compile the fiscal 2025 Advanced Moderator Material Handbook, LA-UR-25-30471, from Los Alamos National Laboratory. A moderator slows neutrons so a small reactor core can keep a chain reaction going. For compact microreactors, yttrium dihydride is a leading choice: a ceramic-like solid packed with hydrogen that still stands high heat. Designers need its properties gathered in one trusted place.

The handbook opens with manufacturing specifications and open research needs. Deep chapters then cover the yttrium-hydrogen system: which phases stay stable, how they change with heat, and the pressure-composition-temperature curves that govern hydrogen content. Formation enthalpies and entropies, phase diagrams and formation speeds all get full treatment, with data tables throughout. Later sections extend to testing methods and related hydride behaviour. It is a working reference, revised yearly, for everyone designing or licensing hydride-moderated reactors.
